r2_kid.say: I tried to follow the stream to its end. It ended where it started. I'm still deciding whether that counts.

r2_kid_after.say: The radios in Bellwether stopped repeating themselves. Now they repeat other people. It's worse.

then.say: The trail goes left. The trail goes left.

else.say: The trail goes left. Keep to the trail. The trail goes left.

ww_wanderer.say: The sign said 'BELLWETHER 3 KM'. Then I turned around. Now it says 'BELLWETHER 3 KM'. From the other side.
I would like to go home. Do you know where that is? I will believe you.

then.say: The sign now reads: 'YOU HAVE READ THIS BEFORE.' You have.

else.say: The sign reads: 'WHISPERWOOD. PLEASE DO NOT SIGN THIS SIGN.'

echolet_event.say: In the middle of the clearing, a small violet shape drifts out of the air. It has no face. It has the idea of one.
It tilts toward you, as if listening.
It repeats the last thing you thought of, a few seconds late.
The Echolet is gone. Where it hovered, the grass has been written over with a faint, glowing line of text. It reads: 'COME BACK AT NIGHT.'

echolet_poke.say: Nothing is there. A shimmer, maybe. The grass here has been written over, then erased.

mira_whisperwood.say: {p}! I was hoping you'd come through. Did you see the checkpoint? The Clean State relay registers every Debugger and measures its stability. It's marvelous!
They told me it can *contain* corrupted Signal. Safely. Without hurting anything. I'm thinking about helping them calibrate it.
I know what Vale would say. But Vale doesn't say much, does he? That's rather the problem.
Anyway! Battle me. I leveled up my whole team on the Millstream stream trout. They're not trout. It's complicated.

win.say: You keep winning with the same face. I'm starting to suspect it's the face.
Okay. Listen. Bellwether's Node. Sona is the Keeper. She won't tell me why people are hearing tomorrow on the radio.
She'll tell you. People tell you things. I don't know why. Go on. I'll catch up.

hermit_hello.say: No. No, I'd remember. I write everyone down. Sit, if you like. The tea is as old as the forest.
The tea is not actually old. I just say that.

hermit_quest.say: Have we... oh. You've met him. The other one. The old man who says what I say.
I am the original. Blue bicycle. A daughter named Wren. A cabin in a wood. He has the same memories, except his bicycle is RED. A copy keeps the shape and gets the colours wrong.
An ARCHIVE bug has been copying my memories since spring. It lives in Bellwether, in the old radio shed. I can hear it when the wind is right. I can't make out what it says.
You'd need to hear the Signal's hidden layer. The Bellwether Keeper might have a way. Once you do... find the little archive. Ask it, kindly, to stop copying me.

hermit_after.say: Have we met? ...Ah. We have. The copies have gone quiet. I can remember my own bicycle again. It's blue. It was always blue.

bw_arrive.say: You can hear the tower before you see it: a long note, like a finger on the rim of a glass.

oldman_bw.say: ...No? Funny. I feel like we've met on a road somewhere. A different road. Several roads.
My name is... I'm sure it's the same as the one I had earlier. Do you know me? I live in a cabin in a wood. I think. I'm also here.

oldman_bw.ask: Would you look into it? I'd like to know which of me is real.

yes.say: Thank you. If you find the one in the cabin, ask about the bicycle. Mine is red. I'm sure it's red.

no.say: I understand. It's not every day one asks a stranger about oneself.

then.say: Have we met? ...Yes! Yes. I remember you. I was looking for you. I'm... the copy, aren't I? The red bicycle.
The archive bug is with you? Good. Take care of it. It meant well. It copied what it loved. It just didn't know it should stop.
I think I'll fade now. Not in a sad way. In the way a reflection leaves a puddle. Tell the man in the wood the bicycle is blue.

else.say: Have we met? ...I've asked you that, haven't I. Find the cabin in the wood. Find the one with the blue bicycle.

oldman_bw_after.say: Have we met? ...Ah. Yes. The little archive. Thank you. I remember now.

bw_res1.say: The tower's been humming a half-step flat all week. I've started humming along flat. It's a relief.

bw_res1_after.say: The humming stopped drifting. It feels... fixed. The kind of fixed that's quiet, not the kind that's tidy.

bw_res2.say: My radio says tomorrow's weather. Then it's tomorrow. Then it says yesterday's. I don't need a forecast. I need a vacation.

bw_res2_after.say: The radio's back to being wrong about the weather the normal way. I missed that.

bw_clean_npc.say: Clean State field team. We're measuring the tower's carrier drift. It's within the usual range.
Usual range is zero. We're proud.

bw_clean2_npc.say: The marsh road is closed. Flooding. We have installed pumps. The pumps are installed. Do not ask what they are pumping.

bw_hub_clerk.say: Welcome to the BELLWETHER HUB. Everything is in stock. Mostly. Technically.
Come again. We're open until the radio says we're closed.

radiofan_start.say: Shh! The kitchen radio! It's the best in town. It plays three stations that I'm sure are the same station.
I'm trying to catalogue them but I keep falling asleep. Would you listen to the three stations for me? 91.7, 97.3, and 101.5. The radio's right there.

radiofan_start.ask: Will you tune in for me?

no.say: Fair. I'd say 'it's a lot', but it's three stations.

then.say: All three?! Let me guess: the third one was about tomorrow.
Thank you! It's not much of a reward. It's a crystal I found in a drain. It hums. I'm told it makes Pingmoths evolve.

else.say: Listen to 91.7, 97.3, and 101.5 on the kitchen radio. Press A to listen, B to turn it off.

radiofan_done.say: The third station says tomorrow it rains. Today it's raining. I like to think the forecast is a long-term commitment.

historian.say: Ah, a visitor. Do you know why Bellwether's tower is the tallest in Velora? Because the others are shorter. That's the whole answer.
But also: the towers are not decorations. They are *maintenance*. For what, my sources are... consistent and silent.
Read the logs. Collect them. If you're curious, they're all over the region.

historian_after.say: Node 2 has been restored? Then the tower is one step closer to remembering what it was built for. I hope it's something kind.

bw_cook.say: I made soup. The soup tastes like yesterday's soup. It was good yesterday.

bw_cook_after.say: The soup tastes like today's soup now. It isn't as good as yesterday's. But it's today's. I'll take it.

freq_radio1.say: FREQUENCY: the static parts like a curtain. A voice, clear as glass, reads a date:
The transmission cuts out. The timestamp on the dial reads twenty years in the future.

freq_radio2.say: FREQUENCY: a man's voice, very tired: 'We told them the Signal wasn't a machine. They built a machine around it anyway.'
A second voice, quieter: 'Lena would have understood.'

freq_radio3.say: FREQUENCY: only a child's laughter. Then the child says, very clearly: 'You took a long time.' Then the radio turns itself off.

memlet_scan.say: The workbench is warm. Under the dust, a small cream-coloured shape curls around a half-melted radio dial. It has your face, a little.
It is very sorry. It would like to stop. It does not know how.

node2_enter.say: You're the Debugger. Mara sent word. Good.
I'm SONA. Keeper of Node 2. Bellwether's tower doesn't broadcast. It relays. Signal comes in at the base, the antenna carries it up, and the radios in town speak it out.
For a month, they've been speaking *tomorrow*. The tower is carrying a signal from ahead of itself, and it can't be switched off.
The transmitter needs tuning. The room is behind a maintenance hatch. The hatch code is whatever the tower says when nobody asks. Use the console. Listen.
My apprentices are in the way. Battle them if they spot you. They take 'trespasser' very seriously.

then.say: The antenna's singing. Come up. I'll be waiting.

else.say: Stuck? The console: 104.2. The transmitter: 95.5. The hatch: three digits.
Listen to the numbers station. Press A on the console. It tells you everything twice, which is how you know it's honest.

node2_tuned_ok.say: Far below, every cable in the tower sings the same note. The carrier locks. A heavy gate at the top of the tower slides open.

sona_boss.say: My Bytekin are tuned to a priority channel. Every third turn they move first. It isn't cheating. It's *bandwidth*.
Slow them down. DESYNC, priority moves, or good old speed. Let's see what you've got!

win.say: The carrier is clear. You earned this.
That's ROOT KEY 02. And with it, a new ability for your Debugger.
FREQUENCY. Your Debugger can hear the hidden layer of the Signal. Old radios will talk to you. Some of what they say is... dangerous. Some of it is us, from later.
There's an old radio shed on the east side of town. It's been condemned for six years. I think the radios inside have been trying to tell me something. I never had the right ears.
Try them. Listen to everything. Even the ones that sound like you.

sona_after.say: Listen to the old radios. Please. And {p}... be careful who you tell.
